messages.content: Help me execute the test runner `runThis` with arguments to set the wait time to 2 minutes and output the logs to a specific print stream `testLogStream`, considering the debuggee name is 'TestDebuggee'?

function.name: runThis
function.description: Executes the test runner with provided arguments and a print stream for logging. It handles the debuggee binding, output redirection, and test execution flow. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

argv.description: An array of strings representing the command-line arguments, to include waittime and debuggeeName. Format: -waitTime, <waitTime>, -debuggeeName, TestDebuggee This is Java Array type parameter in string representation. The list elements are of type String; they are not in string representation.

out.description: The PrintStream to output the logs to. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

message.reasoning: We need to call the function runThis with argv and out. The argv should be an array of strings: "-waitTime", "2", "-debuggeeName", "TestDebuggee". Wait time is 2 minutes? The argument expects waitTime value maybe in seconds? But we just pass "2" as string. The out is "testLogStream". So we call functions.runThis({argv:"-waitTime, 2, -debuggeeName, TestDebuggee", out:"testLogStream"}). But the format: "argv: string" expects a string representation of Java array. The example says: "An array of strings representing the command-line arguments, to include waittime and debuggeeName. Format: -waitTime, <waitTime>, -debuggeeName, TestDebuggee This is Java Array type parameter in string representation. The list elements are of type String; they are not in string representation." So we need to provide a string like "-waitTime, 2, -debuggeeName, TestDebuggee". That is the string representation of the array. So we call functions.runThis({argv:"-waitTime, 2, -debuggeeName, TestDebuggee", out:"testLogStream"}). Let's produce that.
